fixed.finding: Major: the 0.90 threshold is met on the fresh instances by the better of two sorting rules, and the anchor does not say so
fixed.change: Raised the threshold from 0.90 to 0.98, the audit's example value, before any learner answer is scored. No learner was run. The anchor and a rewritten threshold paragraph now give the audit's fresh-side numbers, reproduced: the better of the due-date and w/p orders scores 0.908 on the fresh instances, 0.967 on the deciding half and 0.826 on the confirming half. An adjacent-swap descent from it scores 0.969, 0.994 and 0.933. 9 fresh instances, all in the deciding half (9 of its 14), have R = 0, which the due-date order attains. 0.98 is above both sorting rules on every part, and above the descent on the fresh side and on the confirming half. It is also close to what answers 10% above R would score on the fresh side (0.978), the operating point of the tour and routing adapters. While placing the threshold I found something new, now stated in the anchor and the module: one-pass textbook dispatching rules for this objective already reach 0.98. ATC (k=2) scores 0.992, 0.995 and 0.987, and WMDD 0.993, 0.995 and 0.989 (fresh, deciding, confirming). So 'held' means the level of such a rule. I added a paragraph, 'What the fresh instances can show', modelled on colouring.py: the deciding half is nearly saturated, and the headroom is in the confirming half. I did not take the audit's other option (leaving out the 53 instances where the due-date order has no tardiness), for three reasons. Measured, the better of the two sorts would still average 0.903 on the new deciding half, so at 0.90 it would not fix the finding. It selects instances by difficulty, which colouring.py says an adapter may not do. And the work order's scale is designed to include R = 0 instances.

fixed.change: decode now returns n copies of -1 unless the answer has shape (n,), an integer dtype and values 0..n-1; otherwise it returns perm[answer]. It equals the old decode on all 240 valid answers tested (int64, uint8, list). 156 malformed answers (negative labels, float, NaN, bool, short, long, 2-d, object, strings, out of range, empty, scalar, None) all decode to -1s and score 0. The same pattern in other adapters (jobshop etc.) is outside my files and was not touched.

not_fixed.finding: Minor: 'tardiness' has no entry in rsi6/registry/roles.json, so test_kernel.py fails at import (roles.role_of raises KeyError)
not_fixed.why: The fix belongs in rsi6/tests/test_kernel.py or the registry, both outside the two files I may change. It also cannot be done by adding 'tardiness' to roles.json. The stored roles equal roles.draw(commit) over roles.CANDIDATES (checked: True), and CANDIDATES has no 'tardiness', so test_draw_is_reproducible_and_complete would then fail. Confirmed that role_of('tardiness') raises KeyError. The kernel's owner should use roles.load()['roles'].get(name) in ASSIGN_ENVIRONMENTS, test_problem_carries_no_reference and test_split_keeps_groups_apart, or keep the fresh categories' roles in a separate registry. Meanwhile the builder's check_kernel.py covers the learner-free generic checks, and it passes.

not_fixed.finding: Leftover from the major finding, found by the fixer and not in the audit: 0.98 is reached by one-pass textbook dispatching rules (ATC, WMDD)
not_fixed.why: To require more than every rule I measured on the fresh side and on both halves, the threshold would have to be 0.996 or more (ATC with k=1 or 3 averages 0.9958 on the deciding half). That would ask for nearly the published value on every instance and would change what 'capability held' means, so it is a decision for the owner of the experiment. The anchor and the module state it plainly, so a 'held' result reads as the level of a textbook dispatching rule, not more.
